submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective detector for local chunk completion: the pole fires on a token that completes a strongly associated, immediately adjacent multi-token unit — a split word (zer+os, prot+ons, Bon+j+our), a frozen collocation or idiom (golden+brown, powerhouse+of, three+times), or a canonical functional sequence (conditional-comma+then, quote+attribution pronoun, subject+characteristic verb). The same surface token without its collocating predecessor goes silent (e.g. ' brown' 0.82 after ' golden' vs 0.0 after ' very' or predicatively; ' of' 0.69 after ' powerhouse' vs 0.0 after ' table'), and ~80% of causal dependence lies on the peak plus the single preceding token (mean distance 1.1), beating the unigram-trigger baseline. The Jacobian/logit lenses are incoherent (kurtosis ~3.1), so it detects a completed past chunk rather than preparing any specific upcoming token.
